model.name: Decision / Approval Record
model.purpose: Capture one authoritative decision or approval instance as evidence, including the outcome, rationale, authorised approver or decider, and the period and conditions of validity.
model.scope_statement: WM-REC-010 is the format-neutral record of a single decision or approval act. It specialises a generic record with decision-specific identity, classification, substance, authority, lifecycle, validity, provenance and evidential controls. It does not model reusable decision logic, the producing meeting, the surrounding administrative case, or master data for persons, organisations or policies.
in_scope: Identity, classification and subject of one decision or approval record, including master-system identifiers, governed IRIs and Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID values.
The decision problem, drivers, options considered, chosen outcome, findings, reasons, conditions, limitations and stated consequences.
Approver and participant roles, source of authority, delegation, quorum or vote, recusal and prohibited ex parte communications where a proceeding applies.
Lifecycle states from proposal through acceptance, rejection, deprecation, supersession, appeal, stay, vacatur or invalidation.
Event time versus record capture or observation time, effective date, validity window and sunset or expiry.
Authenticity, integrity, reliability and usability of the record, including attestation, signatures or equivalent seals, completeness of rulings, and confirmation that the decision was implemented.
Access, security classification, disclosure exceptions, retention, legal hold and authorised disposition of the decision record.
Alignments to records-management, provenance, metadata and decision-modelling standards without claiming conformance.
Exceptional paths with primary support, including initial, recommended and tentative decisions and emergency omission of a recommended decision in formal adjudication.
out_of_scope: Reusable, executable decision logic, decision tables, decision requirements diagrams and FEEL expressions belonging to OMG DMN rather than to an instance record.
The meeting, hearing or sitting as an activity (WM-ACT-025); this model only records decisions those activities may produce.
The administrative case or public-service file as a whole (WM-POL-017); this model is the decision instrument that may end or change such a case.
Generic records-management metadata already owned by parent WM-REC-001 except where decision-specific specialisation is required.
Master identity of persons, organisations, software agents, roles, policies, statutes or assets; those are referenced, not duplicated.
Workflow or BPMN process instances, task queues and maker-checker engine traces as process execution, except as provenance of how this record was generated.
Full judicial opinion, case-law citation or Akoma Ntoso judgment ontologies; court orders may align here as a decision record but legal-research models remain siblings.
Clinical decision-support events, FHIR clinical impressions and medical-device alarms.
Qualified electronic-signature product profiles (eIDAS/ETSI) and GDPR Article 22 automated-decision rights, which lack primary support in this source set and are recorded as gaps.

boundary_notes.distinction: WM-REC-001 owns recordhood, capture, metadata and disposition in general. WM-REC-010 extends that record with a single decision outcome, rationale, authorised approver and validity. Do not re-specify the entire records-management stack here.

A meeting is an activity that may produce one or more decision records. The meeting minutes or sitting are not the decision record; the decision record is the separable, citable outcome with approver and effect.
An administrative case is the file or matter. Decisions are the instruments by which the case is granted, denied, varied or closed. This model is the instrument, not the case aggregate.

DMN specifies repeatable business-decision logic that can be validated and executed. WM-REC-010 records a particular authorised instance (who decided what, why, with what validity). A DMN model may be cited as the method used; it is not the approval record.
A policy or rule is the standing authority or criterion. This record is an instance application, grant, denial or interpretation under that authority, with a time-bounded effect.

PROV supplies provenance types (entity, activity, agent, generation, attribution, delegation, invalidation). The decision record is a PROV entity generated by a deciding activity and attributed to agents. PROV does not define approval semantics, findings or validity windows.

sources.title: ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation — Records management — Part 1: Concepts and principles
sources.relevance: Normative records-management concepts: records and metadata, assigned responsibilities, records controls, and processes for creating, capturing and managing records regardless of structure or form.

sources.title: ISO 23081 Metadata for records (ISO 23081-1:2017 principles; ISO 23081-2:2021 conceptual and implementation issues)
sources.relevance: Primary statement that records metadata must support integrity, authenticity, reliability and usability, and must tell who did what to which digital object across the record's life.

sources.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
sources.relevance: Domain-agnostic provenance for the decision record as an entity: generation and invalidation times, usage of input entities, attribution and association of agents, delegation (actedOnBehalfOf), identifiers and derivation/revision.

sources.title: Decision Model and Notation (DMN) Specification Version 1.5
sources.relevance: Defines precise, often executable specification of repeatable business decisions. Used as an alignment boundary: DMN is decision logic, not the authorised instance record with approver and validity.

sources.title: 5 U.S.C. § 557 Initial decisions; conclusiveness; review by agency; submissions by parties; contents of decisions; record
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (Office of the Federal Register)
sources.version_or_date: Administrative Procedure Act; page last reviewed 2016-08-15
sources.relevance: Normative contents of an adjudicative decision record: findings, conclusions and reasons on material issues; the rule, order, sanction, relief or denial; initial, recommended and tentative grades; appeal and agency review; inclusion of all such decisions in the record; ex parte communication rules and docketing.

sources.title: DCMI Metadata Terms
sources.relevance: Cross-domain metadata properties for identifier, title, creator, contributor, issued, dateAccepted, modified, valid, accessRights, provenance, replaces, isReplacedBy, source, rights and rightsHolder.

sources.title: Markdown Architectural Decision Records (MADR)
sources.relevance: Operational template for any important decision record: status vocabulary (proposed, rejected, accepted, deprecated, superseded), decision-makers, consulted and informed roles, context, drivers, options, outcome, consequences and confirmation.

sources.title: Documenting Architecture Decisions
sources.relevance: Canonical lightweight ADR: one decision per record; sequential identifiers not reused; Context, Decision, Status and Consequences; proposed/accepted/deprecated/superseded; keep superseded records rather than deleting them.

sources.title: ISO 15489 (DCC Standards Watch briefing)
sources.relevance: Secondary exposition of record characteristics and the capture–registration–classification–access–disposition process chain. Used only to surface process detail; version predates ISO 15489-1:2016.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How a decision or approval record is identified, named, typed and bounded to a subject, jurisdiction and applicability, independently of storage format.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 requires identifiable records and metadata regardless of form; PROV and DCMI require stable identifiers; Nygard requires sequential, non-reused decision identifiers. Classification prevents collapsing approvals, denials, architectural choices and adjudicative orders into one undifferentiated blob.

layers.name: Record identity
layers.description: Authoritative identifiers, titles and language of the decision record.

findings.name: Decision record identifiers
findings.description: Each decision record needs an authoritative master-system identifier when one exists, else a governed global IRI, else a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Dates, titles and file names are not identifiers. Nygard sequential numbers must not be reused after supersession.

questions.text: What identifier does the authoritative originating system assign to this decision record, and which system is the master?
What governed global identifier or IRI is published for interchange if the record is shared beyond the master system?
If no master or governed IRI exists, what UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign, and when was it assigned?
What local sequential or classified decision number is used for human citation, and has that number been retired rather than reused after supersession?

data_elements.name: Master-system identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the system of record that first captured the decision.

data_elements.name: Governed global IRI
data_elements.description: Persistent IRI used for publication and cross-system reference.

data_elements.name: Dimension UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master or governed IRI is available.

data_elements.name: Local serial number
data_elements.description: Monotonic local number or classified sequence used for citation; not reused.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identifiers are reference values bound to the record entity. They are not a separate artefact type unless an identifier-registry extract is later attached by a sibling registry model.

findings.name: Title, language and alternative names
findings.description: A short noun-phrase title representing the problem and chosen solution, plus language and any alternative citations. DCMI title and alternative apply; Nygard and MADR require a short representative heading.

questions.text: What short title names this decision in terms of the problem solved and the outcome chosen?
In which language or languages is the authoritative text of the decision expressed?
What alternative names, docket numbers or popular citations should retrieve the same record without becoming identifiers?

data_elements.name: Title
data_elements.description: Short noun-phrase heading for the decision record.

data_elements.name: Primary language
data_elements.description: Language tag of the authoritative decision text.

data_elements.name: Alternative titles or citations
data_elements.description: Other human labels that refer to the same record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Title and language are intrinsic descriptive metadata of the record, not a standalone artefact.

layers.name: Type, subject and jurisdiction
layers.description: What kind of decision this is, what it is about, and where it applies.

findings.name: Decision and approval kind
findings.description: The record must distinguish outcome kinds (approve, deny, approve with conditions, defer, revoke, vacate, stay) from domain kinds (architectural, administrative-adjudicative, operational, corporate). DMN covers repeatable operational logic and must not be used as the instance type.

questions.text: Is the recorded act an approval, denial, conditional approval, deferral, revocation, stay, vacatur, or another controlled outcome kind?
Is this an architectural, administrative-adjudicative, operational, corporate, or other domain kind of decision?
Does this record an authorised instance, or is the user actually describing reusable DMN decision logic that belongs in a sibling model?

data_elements.name: Outcome kind
data_elements.description: Controlled code for approve, deny, conditional, defer, revoke, stay, vacate or equivalent.

data_elements.name: Domain kind
data_elements.description: Controlled code for the decision's domain class.

data_elements.name: Linked DMN model reference
data_elements.description: Optional reference to reusable decision logic used to produce or constrain this instance.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Kind codes are classification values. Any DMN model is a referenced sibling artefact, not a payload of this finding.

findings.name: Subject, jurisdiction and applicability
findings.description: The decision must name the matter, case, asset, design or person it binds, the jurisdiction or organisation whose authority is exercised, and any spatial or organisational scope of effect. DCMI coverage, spatial, temporal and DCMI Jurisdiction support this without treating location as identity.

questions.text: What case, request, design problem, asset, licence, person or other subject does this decision bind?
Which legal or organisational jurisdiction is the source of the power being exercised?
Where, to whom and to which systems or territories does the decision apply, and are there explicit out-of-scope exclusions?

data_elements.name: Subject references
data_elements.description: References to the matters or entities bound by the decision.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction
data_elements.description: Legal or organisational jurisdiction exercising authority.

data_elements.name: Applicability scope
data_elements.description: Spatial, organisational or system scope of effect, including exclusions.

artifacts.name: Applicability or territorial schedule
artifacts.description: Optional schedule listing sites, systems, classes of person or territories bound by the decision.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Inherit the decision record's master identifier plus a fragment or child artefact identifier.

bundles.name: Decision substance
bundles.description: The problem, forces, options, chosen outcome, reasons, conditions and consequences that make the record intelligible and reviewable.
bundles.rationale: Nygard and MADR require context, decision and consequences. APA § 557 requires findings, conclusions and reasons on all material issues plus the resulting rule, order, sanction, relief or denial. Without substance the record cannot support later trust or appeal.

layers.name: Problem, drivers and options
layers.description: Neutral statement of the situation, the forces that matter, and the options that were actually considered.

findings.name: Context, problem and decision drivers
findings.description: A value-neutral context and problem statement, optionally framed as questions, plus the drivers or forces in tension. MADR treats drivers as optional; APA proceedings instead receive proposed findings from parties.

questions.text: What problem or question was the decision required to resolve, stated without arguing for the chosen option?
Which legal, technical, political, financial, safety or other drivers constrained the choice?
Which material issues of fact, law or discretion were presented on the record and therefore require a ruling?

data_elements.name: Problem statement
data_elements.description: Neutral description of the situation requiring a decision.

data_elements.name: Decision drivers
data_elements.description: Forces, requirements or constraints that shaped the choice.

data_elements.name: Material issues
data_elements.description: Issues of fact, law or discretion that must be ruled on.

artifacts.name: Context and problem narrative
artifacts.description: The written context section or equivalent statement of the case.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Child artefact of the decision record; versioned with the record, not independently reused as a decision.

findings.name: Considered options
findings.description: The options actually evaluated, including rejected options. MADR records option titles and optional pros and cons. Keeping rejected options is part of reliability: the record should reflect the transaction, not only the winner.

questions.text: Which options were considered, including the option to do nothing or to defer?
What advantages and disadvantages were recorded for each option?
Which options were eliminated by a knock-out driver, and which driver eliminated them?

data_elements.name: Considered options
data_elements.description: Structured list of options evaluated.

data_elements.name: Chosen option identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the option selected, if options were enumerated.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Options are structured fields inside the decision narrative. They become a separate artefact only if an options paper or business-case annex is captured as evidence.

layers.name: Outcome, reasons and conditions
layers.description: What was decided, why, under what conditions, and with what consequences.

findings.name: Decision outcome statement
findings.description: The operative response, in active voice, stating the rule, order, sanction, relief, denial or chosen option. APA requires this as part of every decision included in the record. MADR records the chosen option and justification.

questions.text: What is the operative text of the decision or approval, stated as an action rather than as a discussion?
What specific relief, licence, change, expenditure, design choice or sanction is granted, denied or ordered?
Is the outcome full, partial or conditional, and which parts of the request remain undecided?

data_elements.name: Operative text
data_elements.description: The binding statement of what was decided.

data_elements.name: Relief or order object
data_elements.description: The thing granted, denied, sanctioned or chosen.

data_elements.name: Outcome completeness
data_elements.description: Whether the outcome is full, partial, conditional or deferred.

artifacts.name: Decision or approval instrument
artifacts.description: The signed or issued order, resolution, approval form, ADR body or equivalent instrument that carries the operative text.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Prefer the issuing system's instrument number; else the decision record master identifier plus instrument role. Sequential ADR numbers are not reused.

findings.name: Findings, conclusions and rationale
findings.description: APA § 557(c) requires a statement of findings and conclusions, and the reasons or basis therefor, on all material issues of fact, law or discretion, and that the record show the ruling on each finding, conclusion or exception. MADR rationale may be shorter but still must justify the chosen option.

questions.text: What findings of fact were made, and on which evidence does each finding rest?
What conclusions of law or discretion were reached, and what reasons or basis support each conclusion?
What ruling was recorded on each proposed finding, conclusion or exception submitted by a party?
Why was the chosen option selected against the recorded drivers, including any knock-out criterion?

data_elements.name: Findings of fact
data_elements.description: Determinations of material fact, each linkable to evidence.

data_elements.name: Conclusions
data_elements.description: Conclusions of law or discretion with reasons or basis.

data_elements.name: Justification
data_elements.description: Narrative rationale for the chosen option.

data_elements.name: Rulings on exceptions
data_elements.description: Disposition of each proposed finding, conclusion or exception.

artifacts.name: Statement of reasons or opinion
artifacts.description: The findings, conclusions and reasons document, which may be the body of an order, an ADR rationale section, or a separate opinion.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Same identity family as the decision instrument, with an explicit document-role of reasons.

findings.name: Conditions, limitations and consequences
findings.description: Approvals often bind only if conditions are met. Nygard and MADR require consequences, including negative ones, because they become context for later decisions. Conditions are constraints on continued validity.

questions.text: What conditions precedent, subsequent or continuing must be satisfied for the approval to take or keep effect?
What quantitative, temporal, geographic or use limitations restrict the grant?
What positive, negative and neutral consequences were recorded as the resulting context after the decision?

data_elements.name: Conditions
data_elements.description: Conditions attached to the approval or order.

data_elements.name: Limitations
data_elements.description: Explicit restrictions on the scope of the grant.

data_elements.name: Consequences
data_elements.description: Recorded resulting context, including adverse effects.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Conditions and consequences are structured clauses of the decision instrument. Separate monitoring plans belong to operational siblings and are referenced, not duplicated.

bundles.name: Authority and participation
bundles.description: Who decided, in what role, under what power, with whose advice, and with which process integrity controls.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 assigns records-management responsibilities. PROV models agents, attribution, association and delegation. MADR records decision-makers, consulted and informed parties. APA § 557 regulates who may decide, appeal, and communicate about the merits.

layers.name: Parties and roles
layers.description: Deciders, approvers, consultees, informed parties and recording officers.

findings.name: Approvers, deciders and participant roles
findings.description: PROV Agents (persons, organisations or software) are attributed the entity or associated with the deciding activity. MADR distinguishes decision-makers, consulted (two-way) and informed (one-way). A software agent may be recorded as decider only when that is the actual responsible party; human authorisation remains a separate fact.

questions.text: Which agents are the decision-makers or approvers, and is each a person, organisation or software agent?
Who was consulted, who was merely informed, and who recorded or registered the decision?
If a system or model produced the outcome, which human or organisation remains responsible, and is that attribution explicit?

data_elements.name: Approver or decision-maker agents
data_elements.description: Agents responsible for the decision outcome.

data_elements.name: Consulted agents
data_elements.description: Agents whose opinions were sought with two-way communication.

data_elements.name: Informed agents
data_elements.description: Agents kept up to date with one-way communication.

data_elements.name: Recorder
data_elements.description: Agent who captured or registered the record.

artifacts.name: Signature, seal or approval block
artifacts.description: Captured names, roles, signature images, digital signatures or equivalent seals of approvers. Product-level qualified-signature profiles are a gap.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound to the decision instrument identifier plus signer agent identifier and signing event time.

layers.name: Power and process integrity
layers.description: The legal or organisational basis for deciding, delegation, collective action, recusal and ex parte controls.

findings.name: Source of authority, delegation and collective action
findings.description: PROV ActedOnBehalfOf records that one agent acted for another. APA distinguishes presiding employees, agencies and responsible employees who recommend or decide. Quorum, vote tally and dual-control are operating questions; dual-control lacks a primary source in this set and must not be treated as a universal requirement.

questions.text: What statute, charter, policy, licence or delegation instrument authorised this agent to make this class of decision?
On whose behalf did the deciding agent act, and is the delegation current, limited or expired?
If the decision was collective, what quorum applied, what was the vote tally, and were abstentions or dissents recorded?
Was a second-person confirmation or segregation of duties required, and is that requirement sourced from local policy rather than this model?

data_elements.name: Authority instrument references
data_elements.description: References to the instruments that confer power to decide.

data_elements.name: Delegation
data_elements.description: PROV-style actedOnBehalfOf relationship with validity bounds.

data_elements.name: Vote tally
data_elements.description: Counts and quorum result when the decision is collective.

artifacts.name: Instrument of delegation or appointment
artifacts.description: The charter, appointment, power of attorney or delegation letter relied upon. Owned by an authority or agent sibling; referenced here.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the issuing authority's instrument identifier; do not mint a new identity from the decision date.

findings.name: Recusal, conflicts and ex parte communications
findings.description: APA § 557(d) prohibits ex parte communications on the merits with persons outside the agency who are involved in the decisional process, and requires placement of such communications and responses on the public record. Recusal and conflict disclosure are necessary operating questions for approver integrity even where APA does not apply; they should be marked jurisdiction-specific.

questions.text: Did any otherwise-eligible decider recuse, and what conflict or interest was disclosed?
Were any ex parte communications on the merits made or received, and were they placed on the record with responses?
From what time did ex parte prohibitions apply for this proceeding, and did any person have prior knowledge that a hearing would be noticed?

data_elements.name: Recusals
data_elements.description: Recorded recusals and disclosed conflicts.

data_elements.name: Ex parte occurrence flag
data_elements.description: Whether a prohibited or reportable ex parte communication occurred.

artifacts.name: Ex parte communication docket entries
artifacts.description: Written communications, memoranda of oral communications, and written or memoranda of oral responses required to be placed on the public record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Proceeding record identifier plus sequential docket entry number assigned by the presiding office.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, time and validity
bundles.description: The status of the decision, the times at which it was made and captured, the window in which it has effect, and the later acts that replace, stay or review it.
bundles.rationale: Nygard and MADR define proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated and superseded. APA adds initial, recommended, tentative, appeal and agency review, and allows emergency omission of a recommended decision. PROV separates generation and invalidation times. DCMI supplies issued, dateAccepted, valid, replaces and isReplacedBy. Event time and ingestion time must be stored separately.

layers.name: Status and decision grade
layers.description: Where the record sits in its lifecycle, including adjudicative grades.

findings.name: Decision status
findings.description: A decision may be proposed until stakeholders agree, accepted once agreed, rejected, deprecated, or superseded by a later record that remains linked. Status is not a date. Accepted substance should be treated as immutable; later change is a new record.

questions.text: What is the current status of this decision record in the proposed–accepted–rejected–deprecated–superseded vocabulary, and are any local extensions in use?
What prior statuses did the record pass through, who changed each status, and at what event time versus ingestion time?
Has the operative text been edited after acceptance, or was a superseding record created instead?

data_elements.name: Status code
data_elements.description: Current lifecycle status of the decision record.

data_elements.name: Status history
data_elements.description: Prior statuses with event and ingestion timestamps.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Status is coded state metadata on the record. History entries are inline events, not a separate artefact type.

findings.name: Adjudicative grade and conclusiveness
findings.description: In hearings under APA § 557, a presiding employee may issue an initial decision that becomes the agency decision unless appealed or reviewed; otherwise a recommended or tentative decision may be required, except where the agency finds on the record that due and timely execution of its functions imperatively and unavoidably requires omission.

questions.text: Is this an initial, recommended, tentative or final agency decision, or does that grading not apply?
Did the deciding body preside at the reception of the evidence, and if not, who is the presiding or recommending employee?
Was the recommended or tentative decision omitted because the agency found on the record that due and timely execution of its functions imperatively and unavoidably required it?

data_elements.name: Decision grade
data_elements.description: Initial, recommended, tentative, final, or not-applicable.

data_elements.name: Presided at evidence flag
data_elements.description: Whether the deciding body received the evidence.

data_elements.name: Imperative omission flag
data_elements.description: Whether a recommended or tentative decision was omitted under the APA emergency clause.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Grade and conclusiveness are legal-state fields of the record. The supporting finding of imperative omission, if any, is text on this record rather than a new artefact type.

layers.name: Time, effect and succession
layers.description: When the decision happened, when the record was captured, when it has effect, and how later records replace or review it.

findings.name: Event time and capture time
findings.description: PROV generation is the completion of producing the entity; invalidation ends it. DCMI issued, created, dateAccepted and modified are resource dates. A calendar date is not an identifier. All timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. Decision event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately.

questions.text: At what date-time did the decision act occur, with seconds and explicit offset or Z?
At what date-time was this record observed, ingested or registered, and is that different from the decision event?
When was the instrument issued, and when was it accepted or last modified as a resource?

data_elements.name: Decision event timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time of the decision act.

data_elements.name: Capture or ingestion timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time the record was registered or observed.

data_elements.name: Issued timestamp
data_elements.description: Time the instrument was issued.

data_elements.name: Accepted timestamp
data_elements.description: Time the decision was accepted.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Timestamps are intrinsic properties. MADR's YYYY-MM-DD date field is aligned as a date-only projection and is insufficient as the stored value.

findings.name: Effective date, validity window and sunset
findings.description: DCMI valid is the date or range of validity of a resource. Effect may start after issuance, be retroactive only where local law allows (nunc pro tunc is a regional exception), or expire by sunset. PROV invalidation ends the entity's generation period; legal expiry of effect is not the same as destroying the record.

questions.text: From when does the decision take legal or operational effect, and is that time different from issuance?
Until when does the decision remain valid, including any sunset, expiry or stated review date?
Is effect claimed before the decision event time, and which local authority permits that retroactivity?
Is the decision currently in force given now, its validity window, stays and supersession?

data_elements.name: Effective-from timestamp
data_elements.description: Start of operational or legal effect.

data_elements.name: Valid-to timestamp
data_elements.description: End of validity or sunset, if bounded.

data_elements.name: Indefinite validity flag
data_elements.description: True when no expiry is stated and the decision remains in force until superseded or invalidated.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity is a temporal property of the record. Conditions that can terminate validity are already modelled as clauses, not as a calendar artefact.

findings.name: Supersession, appeal, stay and invalidation
findings.description: Nygard keeps superseded records and points to the replacement. DCMI replaces and isReplacedBy encode that link. APA provides appeal to the agency and agency review on motion, with power to limit issues. PROV invalidation records the end of the entity. Stay, remand and vacatur are distinct from deletion of the record.

questions.text: Which later decision record supersedes or replaces this one, and which earlier records does this one replace?
Has an appeal or agency review been taken, within what time, on which issues, and with what result?
Is the effect stayed, remanded or vacated, and does the underlying record remain as evidence?
If the decision entity was invalidated, at what time and by which activity did invalidation occur?

data_elements.name: Replaces
data_elements.description: Earlier decision records this record replaces.

data_elements.name: Superseded by
data_elements.description: Later decision records that replace this one.

data_elements.name: Appeal or review status
data_elements.description: Whether and how the decision has been appealed or reviewed.

data_elements.name: Invalidation
data_elements.description: PROV invalidation time, activity and reason if the entity has ended.

artifacts.name: Appeal, stay or reviewing-body instrument
artifacts.description: The notice of appeal, stay order, remand or reviewing decision that changes the effect of this record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier assigned by the reviewing body; linked here by reference rather than overwriting the original decision identity.

bundles.name: Evidence, provenance and quality
bundles.description: How the record was generated, what it used, whether it is authentic and complete, and how implementation can be confirmed.
bundles.rationale: ISO 23081 requires metadata that supports authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability and that records who did what to which object. PROV supplies generation, usage, derivation, attribution and bundles for provenance of provenance. APA requires the record to show each ruling. MADR adds optional confirmation of compliance.

layers.name: Generation and inputs
layers.description: The activity that produced the record and the entities it used.

findings.name: Generating activity, used entities and derivation
findings.description: A decision record is a PROV entity generated by a deciding activity that used submissions, evidence, prior decisions, models or meeting records. Derivation and revision relate a later record to an earlier one without implying that usage alone is sufficient. Bundles support provenance of provenance.

questions.text: Which activity generated this decision record, and over what interval did that activity run?
Which evidence, submissions, prior decisions, models or other entities were used in making the decision?
From which prior records or drafts is this record derived or revised, and is a PROV bundle available for those assertions?

data_elements.name: Generating activity
data_elements.description: The PROV activity that produced the record.

data_elements.name: Used entities
data_elements.description: Inputs used by the deciding activity.

data_elements.name: Derived from
data_elements.description: Prior entities from which this record is derived.

artifacts.name: Provenance bundle
artifacts.description: Optional bundled provenance assertions about the decision record, enabling provenance of provenance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: PROV bundle identifier distinct from the decision entity identifier.

findings.name: Source meeting, hearing or proceeding
findings.description: Meetings may produce decision records. APA proceedings produce a record that includes all initial, recommended and tentative decisions. The meeting or hearing identity lives in WM-ACT-025 or a proceeding sibling; this finding only stores the link and the extract that proves the decision was taken.

questions.text: Which meeting, hearing or proceeding produced this decision, and what is that activity's identifier?
What extract of minutes, transcript or docket shows the motion, vote or ruling?
Was the decision first given orally and only later memorialised, and is contemporaneous capture incomplete?

data_elements.name: Source activity identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the meeting, hearing or proceeding that produced the decision.

data_elements.name: Oral-first flag
data_elements.description: True when the decision was announced orally before the record was captured.

artifacts.name: Minutes or transcript extract
artifacts.description: The portion of minutes, transcript or docket that evidences the decision act.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier of the source meeting or proceeding plus locator or timestamp range.

layers.name: Integrity and quality
layers.description: Whether the record is authentic, complete, unaltered and usable, and how compliance with it can be confirmed.

findings.name: Authenticity, integrity, reliability and usability
findings.description: ISO 23081 metadata must support assertions of integrity, authenticity, reliability and usability and record actions on the digital object. Fixity, unauthorised-alteration protection and the ability to present the record in context are therefore in scope for this specialised record, without restating the whole of WM-REC-001.

questions.text: Can it be shown that this record is what it purports to be, created or sent by the purported agent at the purported time?
What fixity or protection against unauthorised alteration is recorded, and have any authorised amendments been logged?
Can the record be located, retrieved, presented and interpreted in its business context, including persistent links to related records?

data_elements.name: Fixity
data_elements.description: Checksum or equivalent integrity value and algorithm.

data_elements.name: Authenticity method
data_elements.description: How authenticity is asserted (process control, signature, witness, system audit).

data_elements.name: Persistent related-record links
data_elements.description: Persistent identifiers linking this record to related records.

artifacts.name: Integrity and authenticity manifest
artifacts.description: Fixity values, signature manifests or system audit extracts supporting authenticity and integrity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Decision record identifier plus manifest version and generation timestamp.

findings.name: Completeness of rulings and confirmation of implementation
findings.description: APA requires the record to show the ruling on each finding, conclusion or exception. MADR confirmation describes how implementation or compliance will be checked. Completeness is a quality property of the decision record; implementation evidence may live in sibling operational models.

questions.text: Does the record contain a ruling on every material issue and every exception presented, and which items are missing?
How will compliance with the decision be confirmed, and by whom?
Has implementation been confirmed, with what result and evidence?

data_elements.name: Completeness assessment
data_elements.description: Assessment that required rulings are present.

data_elements.name: Confirmation
data_elements.description: Method, due time, status and evidence of implementation or compliance checks.

artifacts.name: Confirmation or compliance evidence
artifacts.description: Review, test, audit or ArchUnit-style check that the chosen decision was implemented.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Child artefact of the decision record or reference to an audit-workpaper sibling.

bundles.name: Access, retention and interoperability
bundles.description: Who may see or use the record, how long it is kept, how it is disposed of, and how it aligns to external standards without false conformance claims.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 and 23081 require access classification and disposition. DCMI accessRights, rights and rightsHolder describe resource-level rights. APA distinguishes public-record placement of ex parte materials and does not authorise withholding from Congress. Interoperability is alignment to DMN, PROV, DCMI and ISO, including recorded conflicts.

layers.name: Access and rights
layers.description: Default access, classification, privacy overlay and disclosure exceptions.

findings.name: Access rights, classification and exceptions
findings.description: Records systems need access classification. DCMI accessRights, rights and rightsHolder apply. Public-law disclosure (for example FOIA) is a regional overlay, not a universal default. Privacy of personal data in reasons, and security classification of commercially or legally sensitive approvals, are first-class operating questions.

questions.text: What is the default access rule for this decision record, and who is the rights holder?
Does the rationale or vote record contain personal data that requires minimisation, redaction or a narrower access scope?
Which statutory or policy exceptions withhold or delay disclosure, and which bodies still have an overriding right of access?
What audit trail is required for reads, exports and failed access attempts against this record?

data_elements.name: Access rights statement
data_elements.description: Statement of who may access the record and under what conditions.

data_elements.name: Security classification
data_elements.description: Access classification code for the record.

data_elements.name: Rights holder
data_elements.description: Agent holding rights in the record.

data_elements.name: Withholding exceptions
data_elements.description: Coded exceptions that restrict disclosure.

artifacts.name: Rights and access statement
artifacts.description: The access-rights or licence statement bound to the record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: DCMI rights statement identifier or child artefact of the decision record.

layers.name: Retention, disposition and alignment
layers.description: How long the record is kept, how it may be destroyed or transferred, and how external standards are aligned.

findings.name: Retention, legal hold and disposition
findings.description: ISO 15489 includes identification of disposition status and implementation of disposition. Destroying a decision record is not the same as ending its legal effect. Legal hold must block disposition. DCC's process list (capture through implementation of disposition) is secondary and version-lagged, so retention rules must be taken from the adopting authority's schedule.

questions.text: Which disposition authority or retention schedule class applies, for how long, and what is the trigger event?
Is the record under legal hold or other freeze that blocks destruction or transfer?
What disposition action is authorised at period end, who may perform it, and has it been carried out?

data_elements.name: Retention schedule identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the governing disposition authority.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Duration or rule for keeping the record.

data_elements.name: Legal hold
data_elements.description: Freeze preventing disposition.

data_elements.name: Disposition action
data_elements.description: Authorised end-of-period action and its execution.

artifacts.name: Disposition authority or retention schedule extract
artifacts.description: The class entry that authorises retention and later destruction or transfer of this decision class.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier of the issuing records authority plus class code; not the decision date.

findings.name: Standard alignments and conflicts
findings.description: This model aligns to ISO records standards, W3C PROV, DCMI terms, OMG DMN and APA decision-content rules. Alignment is not conformance. Conflicts include MADR date granularity versus RFC 3339, ADR immutability versus agency amendment practice, APA mandatory findings versus MADR optional sections, and DMN executable logic versus instance approval records.

questions.text: Which external profiles does this instance claim to align to, and is any conformance actually certified?
Which known mapping conflicts apply to this instance, such as date-only ADR fields or missing APA findings?
If the record is exchanged, which projection (for example PROV, DCMI, ADR template, or agency order schema) is the payload, without treating that projection as the semantics?

data_elements.name: Aligned profiles
data_elements.description: External standards or templates this instance is mapped to.

data_elements.name: Conformance claimed flag
data_elements.description: Whether a formal conformance claim is made; default false.

data_elements.name: Mapping conflicts
data_elements.description: Recorded conflicts between this instance and an aligned profile.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Alignment flags and conflict notes are metadata about the record's mapping to external standards, not a separate interchange artefact. Actual payloads are projections owned by interface layers.

functions.name: Capture decision record
functions.description: Create and register a decision or approval record with identity, context, participants and capture time distinct from event time.
outputs: new decision record in proposed or captured status
preconditions: A deciding activity has occurred or is being proposed.
The capturing agent is authorised to register records.
effects: A persistently identified record exists.
Provenance generation and capture metadata are set.

functions.name: Classify and register
functions.description: Assign outcome kind, domain kind, subject links, jurisdiction and access classification, and register the record in the records system.
preconditions: Controlled vocabularies for kind and classification are available.
effects: The record is retrievable by class, subject and jurisdiction.
Access classification is bound.

functions.name: Record approval or denial
functions.description: Set the operative outcome, reasons, conditions and approver attestations, and transition status to accepted or rejected.
preconditions: Approvers are identified and authorised for this class.
Material issues requiring a ruling are listed where an adjudicative grade applies.
effects: Outcome kind and justification become part of the record.
Status becomes accepted or rejected.
Substance is treated as immutable thereafter except via supersession.

functions.name: Evaluate current validity
functions.description: Determine whether the decision is in force at an evaluation time given effective-from, valid-to, conditions, stays and supersession.
preconditions: Event and validity timestamps use RFC 3339 with offset or Z.
effects: A time-specific validity assessment is available without altering the record.

functions.name: Supersede decision
functions.description: Create a successor record that replaces this one, keep the original, and set replaces/isReplacedBy links. Sequential local numbers are not reused.
outputs: updated succession links on both records
preconditions: The original record exists and is not destroyed.
The successor has its own identity.
effects: Original status becomes superseded or deprecated.
Both records remain as evidence.
Current-validity evaluation follows the successor.

functions.name: Review or appeal decision
functions.description: Record an appeal or agency review, optional issue limitation, and the reviewing body's result.
preconditions: An appeal or review path applies in the governing jurisdiction or policy.
Time for appeal has been assessed against local rules.
effects: Conclusiveness may change.
The original record remains part of the proceeding record.

functions.name: Stay or invalidate effect
functions.description: Stay, vacate or invalidate the effect of a decision without treating that act as deletion of the evidence record.
preconditions: The actor has authority to stay or invalidate.
effects: Effect is suspended or ended.
The record remains retrievable as evidence unless a separate disposition action applies.

functions.name: Attest authenticity and integrity
functions.description: Bind signatures or equivalent seals and record fixity so the record can support authenticity, integrity, reliability and usability assertions.
preconditions: Operative text is complete enough to freeze.
Signers are the recorded approvers or their delegates.
effects: Unauthorised alteration is detectable.
Who signed what, and when, is part of the record.

functions.name: Apply retention and disposition
functions.description: Assign a retention class, honour legal holds, and execute authorised destruction or transfer only when due.
preconditions: No blocking legal hold is active.
effects: The record is retained, transferred or destroyed according to the schedule.
Ending legal effect is not implied by disposition unless separately recorded.

functions.name: Disclose or restrict access
functions.description: Apply access rights, redaction and statutory withholding, and audit access, including placement of ex parte materials on the public record when required.
preconditions: Access classification and rights holder are set.
effects: Disclosure occurs only within rights and exceptions.
Access attempts are auditable.

composition.purpose: Specialise the parent record model with decision outcome, rationale, approver and validity rather than duplicating generic recordkeeping.
Link to the meeting or sitting that produced the decision record without absorbing minutes or attendance.
Point to the administrative case that this decision grants, denies, varies or closes; the case composes decision records.
Cite reusable decision logic or tables used to produce an instance without treating DMN as the approval record.

composition.target: W3C PROV Entity, Activity and Agent
composition.purpose: Express generation, usage, attribution, delegation and invalidation of the decision record.
Map identifier, title, creator, issued, dateAccepted, valid, accessRights, provenance, replaces and isReplacedBy.
Identify approvers, consultees, informed parties, recorders and reviewing bodies without duplicating person or organisation master data.

composition.target: Policy, statute or delegation instrument model
composition.purpose: Cite the standing authority under which the instance decision is taken.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the records-management authority or record owner accountable for this Dimension's decision-record package.
Publish the controlled vocabularies for outcome kind, domain kind, status, decision grade and access classification used by the package.
Name the master identity system for decision instruments and the fallback UUID or ULID assignment rule.
Bind a retention schedule class for decision and approval records before production use.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a governed IRI namespace owned by the adopting Dimension for published decision records, and map to http://purl.org/dc/terms/ and http://www.w3.org/ns/prov# only as alignments. Do not treat file paths, Markdown filenames, collection names or calendar dates as identifiers.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical identity order is master-system identifier, then governed IRI, then Dimension UUID or ULID.
Timestamps are stored in RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z; date-only ADR fields are projections.
One record carries one operative decision; additional decisions are additional records.
Accepted or final operative text is canonical; narrative translations are alternates, not replacements.
patch_rules: Do not silently patch accepted operative text, findings or outcome kind; issue a successor record and link replaces/isReplacedBy.
Metadata patches are allowed for access classification, retention class, fixity manifests and typographical identifiers when an audit entry records the patch.
Status transitions append history; they do not erase prior statuses.
compatibility_rules: Consumers must tolerate missing optional MADR sections and missing APA grades when the grade is not-applicable.
A later Dimension may add local status values but must preserve the core proposed/accepted/rejected/deprecated/superseded meanings.
Alignment to DMN, PROV or DCMI must not be advertised as conformance unless independently evidenced.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system instrument or docket identifier.
Governed global identifier or IRI for published artefacts.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when neither master nor IRI exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Store event time and observation or ingestion time separately as RFC 3339 values with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; never use a date as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Local serials are monotonic and never reused after supersession; artefact role names (instrument, reasons, signature-block, ex-parte-docket, integrity-manifest) are suffixes or child identifiers, not replacements for the record id.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Freeze fixity when the operative text is accepted or issued; authorised amendments after freeze require a logged patch or a successor record, consistent with authenticity and integrity metadata.

policies: Treat accepted or final decision substance as immutable evidence; change effect through supersession, appeal, stay or invalidation, not overwrite.
Separate decision event time from record capture time in every write path.
Deny casual deletion; allow destruction or transfer only under a disposition authority and never while a legal hold is active.
Default to least-privilege access, with audit of sensitive reads and with public-record placement only where the governing law or policy requires it.
Do not claim ISO, DMN, PROV or DCMI conformance from mapping alone.

read: Return current status, in-force evaluation at a supplied time, and succession links.
Apply access classification, redaction and withholding exceptions before payload release.
Record audit events for reads of restricted decision records.
create: Require an authorised capturer, an event timestamp, and at least one identified approver or a proposed-status placeholder.
Assign identity according to the identity priority.
Set capture or ingestion timestamp at write time.
update: Permit metadata updates for classification, access, retention, fixity and status history.
Reject in-place edits to accepted operative text, findings or outcome kind unless the caller is creating a successor.
Require reason and actor on every status change.
delete: Do not hard-delete as a user action.
Permit only authorised disposition after retention and legal-hold checks.
Keep a destruction or transfer certificate reference when disposition is executed.

roles.name: Decision-maker or approver
responsibilities: Exercise delegated authority to accept, reject or condition the outcome.
Disclose conflicts and recuse where required.

roles.name: Recorder or records officer
responsibilities: Capture, classify and register the record.
Keep event time and ingestion time distinct.
Maintain persistent links to related records and source activities.

roles.name: Record owner or records-management authority
responsibilities: Own the retention schedule class and access classification scheme.
Monitor authenticity, integrity and usability over time.

roles.name: Reviewing or appellate authority
responsibilities: Hear appeals or reviews within competence.
Issue stay, remand, affirm or replace instruments as new records.
Limit issues on notice where the governing procedure allows.

roles.name: Auditor or access officer
responsibilities: Place required ex parte materials on the public record.
Test that in-force evaluation respects validity windows and succession.

access.default_rule: Need-to-know within the owning organisation or proceeding; public disclosure only where a rights statement or statute requires it, with personal data minimised.
exceptions: Public-record placement of ex parte communications and responses in APA-covered proceedings.
Statutory withholding or redaction of legally privileged, personal or security-classified content.
Oversight bodies that retain access even when public disclosure is withheld, including the APA rule that the ex parte subsection is not authority to withhold information from Congress.
Emergency or sealed decisions whose existence may be known while substance remains restricted for a stated period.
audit_requirements: Log create, status change, patch, read of restricted records, export, failed access and disposition.
Retain access logs according to the same or a longer class than the decision record.
Bind audit events to actor identity, event timestamp and ingestion timestamp.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md for Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL.
Read the Specification URL for canonical semantics of WM-REC-010.
Read the Processes URL for capture, approval, supersession, appeal, access and disposition.
Read the Interface URL and Storage type URL only as projections, never as the model.

coverage.claim: WM-REC-010 can be operated as a format-neutral specialised record for one authorised decision or approval instance, covering identity, substance, approver authority, validity, provenance and recordkeeping controls, by aligning ISO 15489/23081, W3C PROV, DCMI terms, APA § 557 and ADR/MADR practice while keeping OMG DMN and parent/sibling models outside its core.

checklist.notes: Master-system id, governed IRI, Dimension UUID or ULID, and non-reuse of local serials; dates excluded as identifiers.
Proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated, superseded plus APA initial, recommended, tentative, appeal, stay and invalidation.
Subject, meeting, case, prior/successor decisions, used evidence, DMN logic citation, and agent roles.
RFC 3339 event versus capture time, issued/accepted, effective-from, valid-to, sunset and evaluation-time in-force.
PROV generation, usage, derivation, attribution, association, delegation and optional provenance bundles.
Record owner or records-management authority, rightsHolder, and approver versus recorder distinction.
Completeness of rulings, confirmation of implementation, immutability of accepted substance, and fixity checks.
Access classification, rights statements, privacy overlay, withholding exceptions and access audit.
Retention schedule class, legal hold, authorised disposition, and prohibition on casual delete.
Alignments to ISO, PROV, DCMI, DMN and APA with explicit non-conformance default and recorded conflicts.
Source of power, delegation, quorum/vote, recusal and APA ex parte rules; dual-control marked as locally sourced.
Context, drivers, options, findings, conclusions, reasons and justification.
Effect window, conditions that terminate effect, stays and supersession distinct from record destruction.
Emergency omission of recommended decisions, oral-then-memorialised capture, recusal, ex parte, retroactive effect and non-human agents, with gaps flagged where primary law was not fetched.

known_omissions: eIDAS/ETSI qualified electronic signatures and trust-service evidence profiles were not fetched and are not specified.
GDPR Article 22 and other automated individual-decision rights regimes were not fetched; software-agent deciders are modelled only via PROV Agent.
Corporate board-resolution statutes, company-law filing numbers and notarisation practices are not in the source set.
Maker-checker or SOX/COSO dual-control is asked as a local policy question, not as a normative requirement.
Akoma Ntoso, LegalDocML and judicial-opinion structure are excluded; court orders may still instantiate this record.
ISO 9001 documented-information controls and ISO 30300 vocabulary were not fetched as primary texts.
ISO 15489-1:2016 full clause text is paywalled; characteristics are taken from ISO 23081 TC46/SC11 and the official 2016 abstract, with DCC 2007 as secondary and version-lagged.
Clinical, safety-case and financial-trade approval specialisations are not modelled.
conflicts: MADR documents a YYYY-MM-DD last-updated date, which is coarser than the required RFC 3339 event and ingestion timestamps and must be treated as a projection.

Nygard/MADR practice treats accepted decisions as immutable and superseded rather than edited; some administrative systems amend orders in place. This model prefers succession and records in-place amendment as a compatibility exception.
APA § 557 mandates findings, conclusions, reasons and rulings on exceptions for covered hearings; MADR treats drivers, confirmation and option trade-offs as optional. Neither profile is universal.
OMG DMN models executable repeatable logic; ADR and APA model instance records. Merging them would falsify both.
DCC briefing describes ISO 15489:2001 and DIRKS; ISO 15489-1:2016 is the current standard and de-emphasises that methodology. Process names from DCC are secondary only.
APA public-record and Congressional-access rules are US-specific and conflict with a default need-to-know private-sector posture.
regional_assumptions: Adjudicative grades, ex parte docketing and emergency omission of recommended decisions are taken from US APA § 557 and do not automatically apply outside US formal adjudication.
Public-records disclosure overlays (FOIA and analogues) are jurisdiction-specific; DCMI accessRights is the generic hook.
ADR/MADR status vocabularies originate in software-engineering practice and are not legal status codes.
ISO 15489/23081 are international but implementation instruments (retention schedules, classification schemes) are always local.
Retroactive (nunc pro tunc) effect is treated as an exception requiring local authority, not as a default.
adversarial_checks: Could this model be collapsed into WM-REC-001? No: parent recordhood is insufficient without outcome, rationale, approver and validity, which are the stated purpose of WM-REC-010.
Could this model absorb DMN? No: DMN is reusable executable logic; this record is an authorised instance. Absorption would hide the approver and validity surface.

Does unioning APA orders and lightweight ADRs over-claim a single type? The union is defensible at the instance-record layer (one outcome, reasons, agents, status, effect) if grades and mandatory findings remain optional-when-not-applicable rather than always required.
Would treating minutes as the decision record lose citability? Yes; meetings may contain many motions. The decision record must be separable, which matches the WM-ACT-025 CONTAINS relation.
Does allowing software agents as PROV Agents silently erase human accountability? The model requires explicit attribution of a responsible human or organisation when a system produced the outcome.
Is oral-only approval a record? Not until captured; the oral-first flag records a completeness gap rather than inventing a contemporaneous instrument.
